sentences.en: Here's today's show.
sentences.zh: 这是今天的节目。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯（Rachel Abrams），这是《The Daily》。

sentences.en: As the government shutdown enters its second day, Democrats are determined to make this growing political fight all about the rising costs of health care.
sentences.zh: 随着政府停摆进入第二天，民主党人决心将这场日益激烈的政治斗争聚焦于不断上涨的医疗成本上。

sentences.en: Today, I speak to my colleagues Margot Sanger-Katz and Shane Goldmacher about why the Democrats are betting on this particular strategy and who is really to blame.
sentences.zh: 今天，我与同事玛戈·桑格-卡茨（Margot Sanger-Katz）和肖恩·戈德马赫（Shane Goldmacher）探讨了为什么民主党人押注于这一特定策略，以及到底该由谁来负责。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, October 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月2日，星期四。

sentences.en: Margot, we are talking to you on the first full day of the government shutdown.
sentences.zh: 玛戈，我们在政府停摆的第一个完整日与你连线。

sentences.en: And Senate Democrats, in explaining why the government is shut down, have said that this is, above all, about surging health care costs.
sentences.zh: 参议院民主党人在解释政府为何停摆时表示，这归根结底是因为医疗成本激增。

sentences.en: And Democrats are basically saying that in some cases, premiums for Americans, some Americans, are going to be doubling.
sentences.zh: 民主党人基本上是在说，在某些情况下，美国人的保费，部分美国人的保费，将会翻倍。

sentences.en: And I want to start there.
sentences.zh: 我想从这里开始谈起。

sentences.en: Is that accurate?
sentences.zh: 这准确吗？

sentences.en: On average, that is accurate.
sentences.zh: 平均而言，这是准确的。

sentences.en: So this applies to people who buy their own insurance.
sentences.zh: 所以这适用于那些自己购买保险的人。

sentences.en: So people, if you don't get insurance through work and you're not in a government program
sentences.zh: 如果你没有通过工作获得保险，也不在政府项目中，

sentences.en: like Medicaid or Medicare, you might go to the Obamacare marketplace and buy your own insurance.
sentences.zh: 比如医疗补助（Medicaid）或联邦医疗保险（Medicare），你可能会去奥巴马医改市场购买自己的保险。

sentences.en: And the government has set up subsidies that help make that insurance affordable for people.
sentences.zh: 政府设立了补贴，帮助人们负担得起这些保险。

sentences.en: And some of these subsidies are set to expire at the end of the year.
sentences.zh: 其中一些补贴即将在年底到期。

sentences.en: And when that happens, it means the amount that people are going to have to pay for their health insurance is going to go up by a lot.
sentences.zh: 一旦发生这种情况，意味着人们需要支付的医疗保险费用将大幅上涨。

sentences.en: On average, KFF, a health research group, has estimated it's like 114% increase.
sentences.zh: 平均来看，健康研究机构KFF估计涨幅约为114%。

sentences.en: But there's actually a lot of variation under the hood.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，具体情况差异很大。

sentences.en: For some really low-income people who have been paying zero for their health insurance, they're going to have to pay somewhere between like $35 and $60 a month.
sentences.zh: 对于一些收入极低、原本医疗保险费用为零的人来说，他们每月将不得不支付大约35到60美元。

sentences.en: But then as you go like up the income scale, if you imagine someone who's making like around $65,000
sentences.zh: 但随着收入水平提高，如果你想象一个年收入在65,000美元左右的人，

sentences.en: a year, that's someone who might have to pay like $20,000 more a year in some markets.
sentences.zh: 在某些市场，他们一年可能要多付2万美元。

sentences.en: So you see these really big effects.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到这些非常大的影响。

sentences.en: They're uneven and they do depend on how much you make, where you live, and how old you are because nothing about Obamacare is simple.
sentences.zh: 它们是不均衡的，确实取决于你的收入、居住地和年龄，因为奥巴马医改没有任何简单之处。

sentences.en: But a lot of people, and particularly people in red states that did not expand Medicaid, are going to be looking at some very large sticker shock if these subsidies expire.
sentences.zh: 但如果这些补贴到期，很多人，特别是那些没有扩大医疗补助的红州民众，将面临非常严重的“价格冲击”。

sentences.en: To hear the Democrats tell it, the reason that they're shutting down the government is because they say Republicans are to blame for these rising health care costs.
sentences.zh: 按照民主党人的说法，他们让政府停摆的原因是，他们认为共和党人应该为这些不断上涨的医疗成本负责。

sentences.en: And the Democrats will not agree to fund the government until Republicans back a spending bill that lowers those health care costs.
sentences.zh: 民主党人不会同意为政府拨款，除非共和党人支持一项降低医疗成本的支出法案。

sentences.en: That's the overall message, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是整体信息，对吧？

sentences.en: So I guess I'm wondering, how do we actually get to this position that we're in in the first place?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，我们究竟是如何走到这一步的？

sentences.en: Well, I think as is the case with many political questions, the answer to that is a little bit tricky.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为正如许多政治问题一样，答案有点复杂。

sentences.en: I think you have to go back to the politics of the Democratic majorities in the Biden era.
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须回顾拜登时代民主党多数派的政治背景。

sentences.en: So as you may remember, the Democrats had both the White House, the Senate, and the House.
sentences.zh: 如你所记得的，当时民主党同时掌控了白宫、参议院和众议院。

sentences.en: So during the pandemic, when Democrats felt like they could spend a lot of money to help prop up the
sentences.zh: 因此在疫情期间，当民主党人觉得他们可以投入大量资金来帮助支撑经济时，

sentences.en: economy, they extended the subsidies into this current system where the help is just much more generous.
sentences.zh: 他们将补贴扩展到了当前的体系中，使得援助变得更加慷慨。

sentences.en: And there was a debate inside the Democratic Party about how long the subsidies should get extended.
sentences.zh: 民主党内部曾就补贴应该延长多久进行过辩论。

sentences.en: A lot of Democrats, including the White House and the Democratic leadership, really wanted to make this a permanent program.
sentences.zh: 许多民主党人，包括白宫和民主党领导层，真的想让这成为一个永久性的项目。

sentences.en: They felt like this was an improvement on the original Obamacare program.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得这是对最初奥巴马医改项目的改进。

sentences.en: It was making insurance more affordable.
sentences.zh: 它让保险变得更可负担。

sentences.en: It was bringing in lots of people who were previously uninsured.
sentences.zh: 它吸引了许多以前没有保险的人。

sentences.en: But they had kind of a small majority.
sentences.zh: 但他们的多数优势比较微弱。

sentences.en: And they had some members in their caucus in the Senate who were pretty conservative.
sentences.zh: 他们在参议院党团中也有一些相当保守的成员。

sentences.en: And one of them was Joe Manchin of West Virginia, sort of the most conservative member of the
sentences.zh: 其中之一是西弗吉尼亚州的乔·曼钦（Joe Manchin），算是民主党党团中最保守的成员。

sentences.en: Democratic caucus.
sentences.zh: 他担心民主党不应该花太多钱。

sentences.en: He was concerned that the Democrats shouldn't spend too much money.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，补贴数百万美国人的医疗保险确实非常昂贵。

sentences.en: And it turns out that subsidizing the health insurance of, you know, millions of Americans is actually pretty expensive.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对需要他的投票来延长这些补贴。

sentences.en: And they absolutely needed his vote to extend these subsidies.
sentences.zh: 因为共和党人永远不会投票支持这些延期。

sentences.en: Because Republicans were never going to vote for these extensions.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 因此，民主党领导层与曼钦参议员达成的妥协是，他们将延长这些补贴，但只延长几年，而不是永远。

sentences.en: And so the compromise that the Democratic leadership reached with Senator Manchin was they would extend these subsidies, but only for a few years, not forever.
sentences.zh: 所以它们最初是有到期日的。

sentences.en: So there was an expiration date on them originally.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，当时也有过一种算计。

sentences.en: And there was also, I think, a calculation.
sentences.zh: 他们特意选择让补贴现在到期，因为他们知道国会将不得不重新审视另一套即将到期的法律。

sentences.en: They specifically chose to have them expire now because they knew that Congress was going to have to revisit another set of expiring laws.
sentences.zh: 特朗普的减税政策也定于今年年底到期。

sentences.en: The Trump tax cuts also were set to expire at the end of this year.
sentences.zh: 民主党人基本上是在赌，他们可能在华盛顿有足够的控制权，

sentences.en: And the Democrats were basically taking a gamble that probably they would have enough control
sentences.zh: 能够与共和党人达成某种交易，即以延长共和党人都想要的特朗普减税政策为交换，

sentences.en: in Washington that they would be able to make some kind of deal with Republicans, where in exchange for extending the Trump tax cuts, which Republicans all wanted, that Democrats
sentences.zh: 让共和党人也同意延长这些奥巴马医改补贴。

sentences.en: would be able to get them to also extend these Obamacare subsidies.
sentences.zh: 当然，后来发生的事情是，共和党人横扫了权力，完全控制了政府。

sentences.en: Of course, what happened is that Republicans swept to power and had full control of the government.
sentences.zh: 所以他们通过了主要的税收和国内政策法案，根本不需要民主党人的任何帮助。

sentences.en: So they passed their major tax and domestic policy bill without needing any help from Democrats at all.
sentences.zh: 民主党人不仅没能让共和党人将这些补贴纳入法案，

sentences.en: Not only were Democrats unsuccessful in getting Republicans to include these subsidies in their
sentences.zh: 而且在抵御其他近一万亿美元的医疗保健削减（主要是在医疗补助计划中）方面也失败了。

sentences.en: bill, but they also were unsuccessful in fighting off almost a trillion dollars in other cuts to health care, mostly in the Medicaid program.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，民主党人在这一切生效时所做的赌注并没有成功。

sentences.en: So clearly, the bet that the Democrats made when all of this went into effect did not pan out.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是事实，但这也是国会经常会做的赌注。

sentences.en: I think that's true, but it's also the kind of bet that Congress makes all the time.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是民主党人会通过带有这些到期条款的法案，希望未来的国会能让他们的临时项目永久化。

sentences.en: It is not just Democrats who pass bills with these expiring provisions, hoping that a future
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果你看看这些补贴在过去几年扩大以来发生的情况，

sentences.en: Congress is going to make their temporary program permanent.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马医改的注册人数增加了一倍多，而且大部分增长都发生在共和党州。

sentences.en: And I think if you look at what's happened since these subsidies were expanded in the last few
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州、佛罗里达州和德克萨斯州的注册人数出现了巨大的增长。

sentences.en: years, enrollment in Obamacare has more than doubled, and most of the increase has been in Republican states.
sentences.zh: 这些人如果突然需要支付更多费用，确实面临失去保险的风险。

sentences.en: Georgia, Florida, and Texas have had absolutely enormous increases in the number of people who are enrolled in this program.
sentences.zh: 而那些中等收入人群（收入略高于6万美元的人）价格涨幅最大的州，也将是像怀俄明州、阿拉斯加州和西弗吉尼亚州这样的共和党州。

sentences.en: And those are people who are really at risk of losing their insurance if they suddenly have to pay a lot more.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为民主党人觉得他们对共和党人有一定的筹码。

sentences.en: And the states that are going to see the biggest increase in prices for kind of middle-income
sentences.zh: 意思是可能有一些共和党人愿意现在延长这些削减，因为这对他们的选民有好处，

sentences.en: people who earn a little bit more than $60,000 are also going to be in Republican states like Wyoming, Alaska, and West Virginia.
sentences.zh: 即使他们第一次没有投票支持延长同样的补贴。

sentences.en: So I think Democrats feel like they have some leverage over Republicans.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Meaning that there might be some Republicans who are willing to extend the cuts now because
sentences.zh: 民主党人认为，也许共和党人实际上会愿意支持这个项目，因为他们的许多选民从中受益。

sentences.en: of the benefits to their constituents, even if they didn't vote to extend the same subsidies the first time around.
sentences.zh: 但这实际上是一个相当大的赌博，因为现在的现实是政府已经停摆，而美国人不知道停摆何时结束。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 而控制政府所有三个分支的共和党人，他们对外声称这是民主党人的错。

sentences.en: Democrats think that maybe Republicans would actually be willing to support this program because so many of their constituents benefit from it.
sentences.zh: 任何时候你让政府停摆，你都在冒很大的风险。

sentences.en: But this is actually a pretty big gamble because the reality right now is that the government is shut down and Americans don't know when the shutdown is going to end.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，民主党人并没有太多的政治控制权。

sentences.en: And Republicans who control all three branches of government, they are out there saying this is the fault of the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们觉得医疗保健对他们来说是一个非常好的议题。

sentences.en: Anytime you're shutting down the government, you're taking a pretty big risk.
sentences.zh: 这是他们过去曾以此竞选并获胜的议题。

sentences.en: And the reality is that Democrats do not have a lot of political control.
sentences.zh: 这是他们觉得选民比信任共和党人更信任他们的议题，这在很多其他问题上是不成立的。

sentences.en: But I think that they feel like health care is a really good issue for them.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他们觉得如果非要有一场斗争，一场引人注目、混乱且会引起高度关注的斗争，他们希望在这一领域进行。

sentences.en: It's one that they have run and won on in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，肖恩·戈德马赫将讲述民主党人上次利用医疗保健在政治上对抗特朗普总统的时刻。

sentences.en: It's one that they feel voters trust them on more than Republicans, which is not true for a lot of other issues.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: And so I think they feel like if they're going to have a fight, a big, prominent, messy fight that's going to get a lot of attention, they want to have it on this ground.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘（Wynna Liu）。

sentences.en: After the break, Shane Goldmacher on the last time Democrats used health care to win the political moment against President Trump.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《纽约时报》游戏中的拼图游戏《Connections》。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢试着捉弄你们。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基（Sam Azersky）。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”（promesthesia）的东西。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的人那样的人制作的。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.

sentences.zh: 回想2017年，民主党感到有些不知所措，因为特朗普同时做了许多不同的事情，并卷入了他们认为的许多丑闻，

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: I mean, it was the first year of his first term.
sentences.zh: 但最终，这些并不是民主党在2018年中期选举（特朗普第一任期的首次中期选举）中竞选的议题。

sentences.en: You think back to 2017 and the Democratic Party was feeling a bit overwhelmed as Trump did so many different things at once and was involved in what they felt were so many scandals
sentences.zh: 他们最终几乎压倒性地竞选的议题是：

sentences.en: and the Mueller investigation and the FBI directors getting fired and all these things.
sentences.zh: 这就是选票上的议题。

sentences.en: And ultimately, those were not the issues that the Democratic Party ran on in the 2018 midterms, the first midterm election of Trump's first term.
sentences.zh: 这次选举是关于医疗保健的。

sentences.en: What they ended up running on almost overwhelmingly.
sentences.zh: 是医疗保健。

sentences.en: This is the issue that is on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 我们如何保护《平价医疗法案》免受我们预知的攻击？

sentences.en: This election is about health care.
sentences.zh: 这是南希·佩洛西（Nancy Pelosi）和众议院民主党人在特朗普和共和党人试图废除奥巴马医改措施时想出的策略。

sentences.en: Was health care.
sentences.zh: 我们必须做的一件事，废除并取代。

sentences.en: How do we preserve the Affordable Care Act from the assault we know it will receive?
sentences.zh: 他们有一个重大的废除并取代的措施。

sentences.en: And this was a strategy that Nancy Pelosi and House Democrats came upon as Trump and the Republicans tried to repeal the Obamacare measure.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: One thing we have to do, repeal and replace.

sentences.en: They had a big repeal and replace measure.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: Repeal and replace.
sentences.zh: 废除并取代。

sentences.en: Repeal and replace.
sentences.zh: 废除并取代。

sentences.en: Repealing and replacing the disaster known as Obamacare.
sentences.zh: 废除并取代被称为“奥巴马医改”的灾难。

sentences.en: It didn't become law, but that didn't matter.
sentences.zh: 它虽未成为法律，但这并不重要。

sentences.en: Democrats still used this issue and said, Republicans want to take away your health care.
sentences.zh: 民主党人仍然利用这个问题说，共和党人想要剥夺你们的医疗保健。

sentences.en: Now that Donald Trump is trying to sabotage Obamacare, I'm running for Congress to protect and improve it.
sentences.zh: 现在唐纳德·特朗普试图破坏奥巴马医改，我竞选国会议员就是为了保护并改善它。

sentences.en: And for all of the controversies of those first couple of Trump years, this is the one that actually broke through on television.
sentences.zh: 尽管特朗普执政头几年充满了争议，但这一个议题确实在电视上引起了轰动。

sentences.en: A year ago today, my own representative, Congressman Tom MacArthur, introduced a legislation that tried to take away health care from millions of Americans.
sentences.zh: 一年前的今天，我自己的代表，国会议员汤姆·麦克阿瑟，提出了一项试图剥夺数百万美国人医疗保健的立法。

sentences.en: I saw Congressman Bishop smiling at the White House after voting to gut protections for pre-existing conditions.
sentences.zh: 我看到毕晓普议员在投票支持削减对既往症患者的保护后，在白宫露出了笑容。

sentences.en: Something inside me broke.
sentences.zh: 我内心有什么东西破碎了。

sentences.en: This is the one that Democratic candidates in every corner of the country ran ads on.
sentences.zh: 这就是全国各地民主党候选人都在竞选广告中使用的议题。

sentences.en: Half the political ads, according to a study after the election in 2018 that Democrats ran half of the ads talked about health care.
sentences.zh: 根据2018年中期选举后的一项研究，民主党人投放的政治广告中，有一半都在谈论医疗保健。

sentences.en: And just remind us, how well did it work for Democrats in 2018?
sentences.zh: 提醒我们一下，这对2018年的民主党人效果如何？

sentences.en: I mean, it worked pretty well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，效果相当不错。

sentences.en: In the House, they won 40 seats and flipped the chamber and were able to be a check in the second half of that first term.
sentences.zh: 在众议院，他们赢得了40个席位，翻转了多数党地位，并能够在特朗普第一个任期的后半段起到制衡作用。

sentences.en: They impeached Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们弹劾了唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: They took power.
sentences.zh: 他们夺取了权力。

sentences.en: Now, into this shutdown fight, what is the thing they want to stop Trump on?
sentences.zh: 现在，在这场政府停摆的斗争中，他们想要在什么问题上阻止特朗普？

sentences.en: What is the thing they want to fight with Trump about?
sentences.zh: 他们想要在什么问题上与特朗普抗争？

sentences.en: Is it about his overreach in one place?
sentences.zh: 是因为他在某个地方越权了吗？

sentences.en: Is it about firings of U.S.
sentences.zh: 是因为解雇了美国联邦检察官吗？

sentences.en: attorneys?
sentences.zh: 是因为调查吗？

sentences.en: Is it about investigations?
sentences.zh: 是因为调查吗？

sentences.en: It's back to that same issue.
sentences.zh: 又回到了那个老问题上。

sentences.en: It's health care.
sentences.zh: 是医疗保健。

sentences.en: And unlike in 2017 and 2018, where the Republicans had tried to act on this issue and failed, the
sentences.zh: 与2017年和2018年共和党试图在此问题上采取行动却失败不同，

sentences.en: current Republican Congress and President Trump have actually made changes to health care policy.
sentences.zh: 当前的共和党国会和特朗普总统实际上已经对医疗保健政策做出了改变。

sentences.en: And so the Democratic Party isn't just running on the theoretical threats of Republican changes to health care.
sentences.zh: 所以民主党不仅仅是在利用共和党对医疗保健改革的理论威胁进行竞选。

sentences.en: They're running on the reality of changes that are set to go into effect.
sentences.zh: 他们是在利用即将生效的现实变革进行竞选。

sentences.en: But just to point out one obvious difference, right now, this is not technically an election year, unlike 2018.
sentences.zh: 但要指出一个明显的区别，现在并不是选举年，这与2018年不同。

sentences.en: But the next election, of course, is a midterm election next November.
sentences.zh: 当然，下一次选举是明年十一月的中期选举。

sentences.en: So with that in mind, how much does this Democratic strategy that we're talking about resemble the 2018 playbook?
sentences.zh: 那么考虑到这一点，我们所说的这种民主党策略与2018年的竞选剧本有多相似？

sentences.en: Well, we don't know for sure, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们还不能确定，对吧？

sentences.en: They have yet to run ads in a lot of these districts.
sentences.zh: 他们还没在许多选区投放广告。

sentences.en: The campaign hasn't been fully formed yet.
sentences.zh: 竞选活动尚未完全成形。

sentences.en: But what you see in this shutdown is the Democrats basically trying to settle on an issue where they know they're on the winning side of public opinion.
sentences.zh: 但你在这次停摆中看到的是，民主党人基本上试图锁定一个他们知道在民意上占优势的议题。

sentences.en: And they're trying to basically lay the groundwork for voters to know one year from now where the two parties are on this.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是在为选民打基础，让他们在一年后知道两党在这个问题上的立场。

sentences.en: And look, Ted Cruz and the Republicans pushed a major shutdown that was a really big deal in 2013.
sentences.zh: 看，泰德·克鲁兹和共和党人在2013年推动了一场重大的政府停摆，那可是件大事。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: Republicans won a bunch of seats in the Congress the next year, right?
sentences.zh: 共和党人在第二年的国会选举中赢得了许多席位，对吧？

sentences.en: So the issue isn't just do you win this temporary argument around the shutdown can also be do you win the long term argument of what your party is seen fighting for?
sentences.zh: 所以问题不仅仅是你是否赢得了围绕停摆的这场暂时性争论，还在于你是否赢得了关于你的政党被视为在为什么而战的长期争论？

sentences.en: And that's very much what the Democratic Party is hoping for, that they can be seen fighting
sentences.zh: 这正是民主党所希望的，他们希望被视为在为医疗保健而战，

sentences.en: for health care, an issue that they've won before on and when they think that they can win again on.
sentences.zh: 这是一个他们曾经获胜，并且认为他们可以再次获胜的议题。

sentences.en: In other words, they're betting that health care is going to be a bigger deal than shutting down the government.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们押注医疗保健比政府停摆更重要。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So how are Republicans responding to that strategy?
sentences.zh: 那么共和党人是如何回应这一策略的？

sentences.en: I think they're chiefly so far responding to the shutdown part of it, which is to say, first off, it's the Democrats who have shut down this government for this issue of health
sentences.zh: 我认为到目前为止，他们主要是针对停摆部分做出回应，也就是说，首先，正是民主党人为了医疗保健这个问题而关闭了政府。

sentences.en: care.
sentences.zh: 医疗保健。

sentences.en: And second, to pivot to areas where the Republican Party is more trusted.
sentences.zh: 其次，转向共和党更受信任的领域。

sentences.en: And that so far has been immigration.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，那就是移民问题。

sentences.en: They've been talking about how the Democrats want to fight for health care for illegal immigrants,
sentences.zh: 他们一直在谈论民主党人如何想要为非法移民争取医疗保健，

sentences.en: although the Obamacare subsidies that are at issue here that the Democrats are demanding be extended do not apply to people who are here illegally.
sentences.zh: 尽管这里涉及的奥巴马医改补贴（民主党要求延长这些补贴）并不适用于非法居留的人。

sentences.en: But that's the focus, right?
sentences.zh: 但这就是焦点，对吧？

sentences.en: And they're doing it to try to send a signal that this is actually not about health care,
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是为了发出一个信号，即这实际上不是关于医疗保健，

sentences.en: but about spending money for people who are here illegally, which polls unpopularly, right?
sentences.zh: 而是关于为非法居留的人花钱，这在民调中是不受欢迎的，对吧？

sentences.en: The Democrats are staking ground on a place that is popular, and the Republicans are trying to change the ground into a place that is unpopular.
sentences.zh: 民主党人在一个受欢迎的阵地上扎根，而共和党人正试图将阵地转移到一个不受欢迎的地方。

sentences.en: Basically, each side is retreating to issues that are winning for them in their own way.
sentences.zh: 基本上，双方都在退回到各自认为能获胜的议题上。

sentences.en: Their own safe spaces, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 可以说，是他们各自的安全地带。

sentences.en: It strikes me that for the strategy to work that you are describing, Democrats need to focus on health care basically for as long as possible, right?
sentences.zh: 我感到，为了让你描述的策略奏效，民主党人需要尽可能长时间地专注于医疗保健，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, basically, is it actually to their benefit to have Republicans refuse to meet them halfway so they can keep kind of pounding on about these rising health care costs and
sentences.zh: 比如，共和党人拒绝与他们妥协，让他们能够继续抨击这些不断上涨的医疗保健成本，并将其归咎于对方，这对他们来说实际上是有利的吗？

sentences.en: blame it on the other side?
sentences.zh: 归咎于对方？

sentences.en: Look, I think that if the Democratic Party could snap their fingers and have Republicans actually negotiate over health care and strike a deal on this, they would take that in a
sentences.zh: 看，我认为如果民主党能打个响指，让共和党人真的就医疗保健进行谈判并达成协议，他们会毫不犹豫地接受。

sentences.en: heartbeat.
sentences.zh: 对于一个他们关心的、民主党选民基础关心的、影响选民的政策，他们绝对会接受。

sentences.en: On a policy that they care about, that the Democratic base cares about, that impacts voters, they would absolutely take that.
sentences.zh: 看，一些共和党人甚至对这一具体政策的谈判持开放态度，即是否应该延长奥巴马医改的一些补贴，因为这确实影响选民。

sentences.en: And look, some Republicans are even open to negotiations on this exact policy, on whether there should be some subsidies extended for Obamacare, because this does impact voters.
sentences.zh: 但共和党人相当一致的是。

sentences.en: But what the Republicans are pretty universal on.
sentences.zh: 我们都明白民主党和共和党在政策上有分歧。

sentences.en: We all understand that Democrats and Republicans have policy disagreements.
sentences.zh: 你从J.D.万斯那里听到的。

sentences.en: And what you heard from J.D.
sentences.zh: 你不能因为政策分歧而导致政府停摆。

sentences.en: Vance.
sentences.zh: 万斯。

sentences.en: You don't have policy disagreements that serve as the basis for a government shutdown.
sentences.zh: 你不能因为政策分歧而导致政府停摆。

sentences.en: Was that as long as the government is shut down, you're getting absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 那是说只要政府停摆，你就什么也得不到。

sentences.en: Do the right thing, open up the people's government, and then let's fix health care policy for the
sentences.zh: 做正确的事，开放人民的政府，然后让我们为美国人民修复医疗保健政策。

sentences.en: American people.
sentences.zh: 美国人民。

sentences.en: Questions?
sentences.zh: 有问题吗？

sentences.en: Shane, do you have any sense about which side has the upper hand right now?
sentences.zh: 肖恩，你觉得现在哪一方占上风？

sentences.en: I think it's really hard to say, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这真的很难说，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, the Democratic Party is fighting on an issue that they think they have the high ground
sentences.zh: 民主党人正在为一个他们认为占据道德高地的议题而战，

sentences.en: that is popular in polling, which is health care and making health care cheaper for Americans.
sentences.zh: 这个议题在民调中很受欢迎，那就是医疗保健，以及让美国人的医疗保健更便宜。

sentences.en: But there's a tricky thing here, which is, in order to show that you're fighting for health care, you kind of have to own that you're shutting down the government to do it.
sentences.zh: 但这里有一件棘手的事情，那就是，为了表明你在为医疗保健而战，你必须承认你是为了做到这一点而关闭了政府。

sentences.en: And voters don't want to see the government shut down for political demands.
sentences.zh: 选民们不想看到政府因为政治诉求而停摆。

sentences.en: And so each day that the government stays shut down and more and more Americans are impacted
sentences.zh: 所以，政府停摆的每一天，越来越多的美国人受到政府停摆的影响，

sentences.en: by the government shutdown, that people start missing paychecks, that parks start closing,
sentences.zh: 人们开始领不到工资，公园开始关闭，

sentences.en: that services stop being offered, it becomes a bigger and bigger gamble for the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 服务停止提供，这对民主党来说就成了一场越来越大的赌博。

sentences.en: Shane, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 肖恩，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: On Wednesday evening, the Trump administration halted billions of dollars in funds for Democratic-led
sentences.zh: 周三晚上，特朗普政府暂停了向民主党领导的州提供数十亿美元的资金，

sentences.en: states, while it readied to lay off scores of government workers, a plan seemingly intended to maximize pain from the shutdown.
sentences.zh: 同时准备解雇大批政府工作人员，这一计划似乎旨在最大化停摆带来的痛苦。

sentences.en: In a series of social media posts, Russell T.
sentences.zh: 在一系列社交媒体帖子中，白宫预算主任罗素·T·沃特表示，

sentences.en: Vogt, the White House budget director, said that the administration had paused or moved to cancel the delivery of about $26 billion in
sentences.zh: 政府已经暂停或取消了约260亿美元的资金拨付，这些资金涉及一系列项目，

sentences.en: previously approved funds across a range of programs, describing the money as wasteful or in need of further review.
sentences.zh: 他将这些资金描述为浪费或需要进一步审查。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court on Wednesday blocked President Trump's efforts to remove Lisa Cook from the
sentences.zh: 周三，最高法院阻止了特朗普总统将丽莎·库克从美联储理事会中除名的努力，

sentences.en: board of the Federal Reserve, at least temporarily stymieing his efforts to reshape the agency as he pushes it to lower interest rates.
sentences.zh: 至少暂时阻碍了他重塑该机构的努力，因为他正推动美联储降低利率。

sentences.en: The court said it would review the administration's efforts to oust Ms. Cook at oral arguments in January.
sentences.zh: 法院表示，将在1月份的口头辩论中审查政府罢免库克女士的努力。

sentences.en: Top former Fed and Treasury officials had warned the court that allowing the president to fire
sentences.zh: 前美联储和财政部高层官员曾警告法院，允许总统在诉讼进行期间解雇库克女士，将扰乱市场并削弱公众对美联储的信心。

sentences.en: Ms. Cook while litigation was underway would roil the markets and undermine public confidence in the Fed.
sentences.zh: 库克女士。

sentences.en: And scientist and conservationist Jane Goodall, who made groundbreaking discoveries about how chimpanzees behave and communicate, has died at the age of 91.
sentences.zh: 科学家兼自然资源保护主义者珍·古道尔，因在黑猩猩行为和交流方面的开创性发现而闻名，已于91岁高龄去世。

sentences.en: When I arrived in Gombe, I had no idea what I was going to do, except that I was going to
sentences.zh: 当我到达贡贝时，我不知道我要做什么，除了我要

sentences.en: try and get the chimpanzees used to me so that I could really learn about what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 尝试让黑猩猩习惯我的存在，这样我就能真正了解它们在做什么。

sentences.en: Goodall observed chimps by living alongside them, on a reserve in what is now Tanzania, beginning in 1960.
sentences.zh: 古道尔从1960年开始，通过与黑猩猩生活在坦桑尼亚的一个保护区内来观察它们。

sentences.en: I've seen a mother laugh when she hears her older child who hasn't paid attention and he hasn't noticed which way she's gone and that the older child is going through the forest,
sentences.zh: 我见过一位母亲在听到她的大孩子因为没注意而不知道她去了哪里，正在森林里呜咽、哭泣时发笑，你知道的。

sentences.en: whimpering, crying, you know.
sentences.zh: 呜咽、哭泣，你知道的。

sentences.en: After months of working to gain their trust, she documented the chimps engaging in behaviors previously thought to be exclusive to people, including making and using tools.
sentences.zh: 在经过几个月努力赢得它们的信任后，她记录了黑猩猩表现出以前被认为仅限于人类的行为，包括制造和使用工具。

sentences.en: Bringing the chimpanzees into people's lives as individuals, as personalities, as creatures with whom we can relate so individually.
sentences.zh: 将黑猩猩作为个体、作为人格、作为我们可以如此个体化地与之产生联系的生物带入人们的生活。

sentences.en: And that in turn has led to a gradual blurring of the line that we used to see as so sharp between us on the one hand and all the other amazing animals on the other.
sentences.zh: 这反过来导致了我们过去认为在我们这一方和所有其他神奇动物之间那条界限的逐渐模糊。

sentences.en: Now that line is very blurry, thanks to the chimps.
sentences.zh: 现在，多亏了黑猩猩，那条界限变得非常模糊了。

sentences.en: Goodall eventually came to advocate for them and other wildlife by founding the Jane Goodall
sentences.zh: 古道尔最终通过创立珍·古道尔研究所（全球最大的保护组织之一）来倡导保护它们和其他野生动物。

sentences.en: Institute, one of the world's largest conservation groups.
sentences.zh: 研究所。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是说他们是不是昏过去才睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
